items.assistant_question: Good to meet you. I’ll help you find a course project that fits what you enjoy and what is realistic for you. What part of what you just mentioned do you enjoy most?
Tell me about a time you kept working on a science thing even after it got annoying or didn’t work right away—what did you do?
When you’re doing a science thing like that, what feels most rewarding: figuring out why something works, getting a result you can show, or seeing it help people nearby?
What’s the biggest limit on a course project for you right now—time, budget, tools, or something else?
What kind of useful thing would feel most worth making for your community: a map, a simple tool, a report, or something else?
With Python and spreadsheets, what’s something you can do on your own right now that would save you time in a project?
What’s a task you’ve already done with Python or spreadsheets that you could teach someone else?
When a project gets a bit unclear, what do you usually do first: make a rough plan, ask someone, or start experimenting?
When a Python or spreadsheet task gets unclear, what do you do first: sketch a rough plan, ask someone, or start testing it?
Think of a time a Python or science project got messy—what did you do next?
When you hit a snag in a science project, what’s the first thing you usually try to get unstuck?
Does that profile feel right overall, or is there one part you’d change?
What part of that profile feels most off to you?
You said live demos to a big room still make you nervous—what kind of presentation feels doable instead?
What usually helps you keep going when a science project gets annoying or unclear?
What part of a science project usually pulls you in most: collecting the data, figuring out what it means, or making the final thing clear to other people?
What would be a good first milestone for your dashboard—like a data-cleaning notebook, a simple chart, or a rough layout?
